description.summary: Neo4j is a native property-graph database with Lucene HNSW vector indexes, Cypher filtering and graph traversal, and separately scoped lexical-vector fusion through Cypher or neo4j-graphrag.
description.description: Neo4j combines native graph storage and traversal, Cypher querying, ACID transactions, vector and full-text indexes, self-managed Community and Enterprise editions, the Infinigraph offering, and managed Aura services. Neo4j 2026.06 supports approximate vector search over node or relationship properties with cosine or Euclidean similarity, generally available scalar quantization, preview binary quantization, and preview vector.default_search_expansion_factor. Community stores indexed embeddings as supported numeric lists; native VECTOR property storage requires Enterprise block format or Aura. Lexical-vector hybrid retrieval has two distinct first-party origins in this record: ranked-list composition written directly in Cypher using weighted reciprocal-rank fusion, and configurable fusion in the separately installed neo4j-graphrag 1.17.0 package whose behavior is bound to release commit 7b69354. Vector-Graph Composition remains a separate Cypher traversal pattern. Operational capabilities distinguish Neo4j-core TLS from host-platform volume encryption and separate AuraDB Free on-demand snapshots from paid-plan export and restore actions.

capabilities.name: Vector Similarity Retrieval
capabilities.statement: Retrieves node or relationship candidates through HNSW vector indexes.

boundary.behavior: Indexes and retrieves vector-bearing Neo4j properties.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j database engine and Lucene-backed vector-index subsystem

availabilityScope.notes: The vector-index capability is generally available. Binary quantization and vector.default_search_expansion_factor are separately scoped Preview features in Neo4j 2026.06. Native VECTOR property storage requires Enterprise block format or Aura; Community can index supported numeric-list properties.

constraints.description: Approximate search must be benchmarked for recall and result completeness.

capabilities.name: Vector Search Expansion Control
capabilities.statement: Configures the vector.default_search_expansion_factor used to query more neighbors than are returned.

boundary.behavior: Scales the vector-index neighbor search while retaining the requested result count.
excludedResponsibilities: Changing the maturity of the generally available vector-index capability

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j 2026.06 vector-2026.06 index provider

constraints.description: Values above 1.0 can increase accuracy at the cost of query time, and defaults depend on the quantization type.

capabilities.name: Filtered Vector Retrieval
capabilities.statement: Applies in-index predicates or outer Cypher post-filtering.

boundary.behavior: Constrains vector candidates through SEARCH WHERE or outer WHERE.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Cypher 25 SEARCH clause and Neo4j vector-index execution

constraints.description: Filter placement changes completeness, supported predicates and cost.

capabilities.name: Full-Text and Vector Fusion
capabilities.statement: Combines full-text and vector candidates through configurable fusion in neo4j-graphrag 1.17.0.

boundary.behavior: Executes lexical-vector fusion through Neo4j GraphRAG for Python.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Separately installed neo4j-graphrag Python package

constraints.description: Quality depends on analyzers, embeddings, candidate pools and weights.

capabilities.name: Cypher Full-Text and Vector WRRF
capabilities.statement: Combines independently ranked full-text and vector candidate lists in Cypher using weighted reciprocal-rank fusion.

boundary.behavior: Executes full-text and vector retrieval branches and fuses their ranks in a user-authored Cypher query.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: User-authored Cypher combining Neo4j full-text and vector retrieval primitives

constraints.description: Source candidate counts, rrfConstant, source weights, tie-breaking and security filtering remain query-defined and workload-specific.

capabilities.name: Vector-Cypher Context Expansion
capabilities.statement: Expands vector-retrieved entities through explicit Cypher traversal.

boundary.behavior: Composes vector retrieval and graph traversal in a user-authored query.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Cypher vector-index retrieval plus graph traversal

constraints.description: Traversal depth, fan-out and context assembly remain workload-defined.

capabilities.name: Enterprise Cluster Replication and Read Scaling
capabilities.statement: Provides replicated primaries and read-scaling secondaries.

boundary.behavior: Provides Enterprise cluster replication and bookmark-mediated causal consistency.
includedResponsibilities: Synchronous replication from the writer to enough primaries before commit
Asynchronous transaction-log replication to read-scaling secondaries
Read-your-own-writes routing through bookmarks when causal consistency is invoked
excludedResponsibilities: Universal replication across Community and all Aura plans
Immediate visibility of recent commits on an unbookmarked secondary

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Enterprise clustering

constraints.description: Secondaries replicate asynchronously and can lag; standard clustering must not be equated with automatic sharding.

capabilities.name: Infinigraph Property Sharding
capabilities.statement: Distributes graph property data across property shards while retaining a logical graph boundary.

boundary.behavior: Provides automatic property sharding through the specialized Infinigraph Enterprise offering.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Enterprise Edition with Infinigraph subscription

availabilityScope.notes: Introduced in Neo4j 2025.12, requires a separate subscription, and is not available on Aura.

constraints.description: Property sharding has feature-specific limitations and must be validated for the target vector-index and access-control workload.

capabilities.name: Lucene Vector-Index Storage and Filesystem Cache
capabilities.statement: Persists Lucene-backed vector-index files and serves them through the operating-system filesystem cache when resident.

boundary.behavior: Stores vector-index files on disk and relies on the operating-system filesystem cache for query-time residency.
excludedResponsibilities: A guarantee that vector queries avoid disk I/O
Neo4j page-cache residency for Lucene vector-index files

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Lucene-backed Neo4j vector-index subsystem and host operating-system filesystem cache

availabilityScope.notes: Aura uses the same product-facing vector-index behavior, but its storage and cache provisioning are provider managed and are not characterized here.

constraints.description: Insufficient RAM for the filesystem cache increases disk reads and can degrade search latency; restart clears the warm filesystem cache.

capabilities.name: ACID Transaction Processing
capabilities.statement: Provides ACID transactions for graph data and vector-bearing properties.

boundary.behavior: Commits transactional data while vector-index visibility follows separate timing.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j transaction engine

constraints.description: Vector-index changes are not searchable inside the creating transaction.

capabilities.name: Community Offline Dump and Load
capabilities.statement: Creates and restores offline database dump archives in Community Edition.

boundary.behavior: Provides offline full dump and load workflows for a Community database.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Community neo4j-admin dump and load tooling

constraints.description: Dump requires an offline database and does not include users or roles metadata.

capabilities.name: Enterprise Backup and Restore
capabilities.statement: Provides full and differential backup and restore workflows.

boundary.behavior: Creates and restores self-hosted Enterprise database backups.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Enterprise backup and restore tooling

constraints.description: Recovery depends on backup cadence and tested restore procedures.

capabilities.name: Aura Paid-Plan Snapshot Recovery
capabilities.statement: Provides provider-managed snapshot, export and restore workflows on supported paid Aura plans.

boundary.behavior: Manages scheduled or on-demand snapshots and plan-specific export, create-from-snapshot, and restore actions inside the Neo4j Aura service boundary.
excludedResponsibilities: A restorable or exportable period for AuraDB Free
Identical recovery actions or retention across paid Aura plans

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Aura managed service

availabilityScope.notes: Scheduled cadence, retention, restore, export, and create-from-snapshot behavior vary across Professional, Business Critical, Virtual Dedicated Cloud, AuraDS Professional, and AuraDS Enterprise. AuraDB Free is excluded because its documented restorable and exportable periods are N/A.

capabilities.name: AuraDB Free On-Demand Snapshot

boundary.behavior: Creates an on-demand snapshot within the AuraDB Free managed-service boundary.
excludedResponsibilities: Paid-plan backup, export, create-from-snapshot, or restore equivalence

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j AuraDB Free managed service

constraints.description: Snapshot lifecycle and any available user action remain provider managed; this capability does not establish a recoverable or exportable retention window.

capabilities.name: Enterprise and Applicable Aura Advanced Access Control
capabilities.statement: Provides role-based and fine-grained graph privileges in Enterprise Edition and applicable Aura tiers.

boundary.behavior: Authorizes graph and administrative operations through roles and privileges.
excludedResponsibilities: A guarantee that vector or full-text indexes return the requested result count under security restrictions

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Enterprise authorization engine and applicable Aura database tiers

availabilityScope.notes: Community provides a smaller authentication and authorization subset; property-based access control is documented for Enterprise, AuraDB Business Critical, and AuraDB Virtual Dedicated Cloud and is not supported for sharded property databases.

constraints.description: Security privileges must be tested with vector and full-text retrieval because index-backed searches can return fewer results under restrictions.

capabilities.name: Self-Managed TLS Transport Protection
capabilities.statement: Provides configurable TLS protection for Neo4j communication channels in self-managed deployments.

boundary.behavior: Configures Neo4j SSL policies and TLS for Bolt, HTTPS, cluster, and backup communication channels.
includedResponsibilities: TLS enablement for supported Neo4j communication channels
Certificate and private-key loading through the Neo4j SSL framework
excludedResponsibilities: Host, cloud-disk, storage-platform, or volume encryption

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j SSL/TLS framework
capabilityOrigin.notes: Neo4j exposes the SSL policy and channel configuration surface; the deployment operator remains responsible for certificates, private keys, trust configuration, rotation, and secure channel enablement.

constraints.description: Certificate issuance, trust, private-key protection, renewal, rotation, protocol selection, and verification of every required channel remain operator responsibilities.

capabilities.name: Self-Managed Storage-Volume Encryption
capabilities.statement: Uses operating-system, cloud-disk, storage-platform, or operator-managed volume encryption to protect self-managed Neo4j files at rest.

boundary.behavior: Protects Neo4j database files and other selected stored artifacts through encryption supplied below the Neo4j DBMS boundary.
includedResponsibilities: Host or storage-platform encryption for selected Neo4j data volumes
Operator selection of encrypted volumes and covered file locations
Platform or operator key-management and recovery procedures
excludedResponsibilities: Automatic coverage of backups, exports, transaction logs, or copied files outside encrypted volumes

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Operating system, cloud disk, storage platform, or operator-managed encrypted volume
capabilityOrigin.notes: The host platform or deployment operator implements at-rest protection; Neo4j documentation recommends volume encryption but this is not a universal Neo4j DBMS-core at-rest-encryption feature.

availabilityScope.notes: Availability and implementation depend on the chosen operating system, cloud disk, storage platform, and operator configuration rather than the Neo4j edition.

constraints.description: Encryption strength, covered paths, key custody, rotation, backup and export coverage, incident recovery, and verification depend on the host platform and operator.

capabilities.name: Aura Managed Encryption
capabilities.statement: Encrypts Aura stored data, backups, intra-cluster traffic, and client connections inside the managed-service boundary.

boundary.behavior: Provides provider-managed encryption in transit and at rest for Aura instances and backups.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Aura and its underlying cloud-provider encryption services

availabilityScope.notes: Customer-managed key availability is tier- and cloud-dependent and is not generalized by this capability.

constraints.description: Key-management options and isolation controls depend on the selected Aura tier, cloud provider, region, and contract.

capabilities.name: Self-Managed Basic Logging
capabilities.statement: Writes general, debug, HTTP, garbage-collection, and edition-dependent operational logs for self-managed deployments.

boundary.behavior: Emits configured server log files for operational diagnosis.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j self-managed logging subsystem

availabilityScope.notes: Query and security logs are Enterprise features; the exact enabled log set and defaults differ by log type.

capabilities.name: Enterprise Metrics Monitoring
capabilities.statement: Exposes DBMS and per-database metrics through Enterprise monitoring facilities.

boundary.behavior: Provides Enterprise metrics through CSV, JMX, Graphite, Prometheus, or Neo4j Ops Manager integrations.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j Enterprise metrics subsystem

constraints.description: Prometheus, Graphite, dashboards, alerting, retention and incident response require separately operated monitoring infrastructure.

capabilities.name: Edition-Scoped Database Partitioning
capabilities.statement: Provides one standard database in Community and multiple standard or composite databases in Enterprise.

boundary.behavior: Partitions administrative and transaction domains through databases and Enterprise composite databases.

capabilityOrigin.implementationBoundary: Neo4j database-administration subsystem

editions: Community Edition: exactly one standard database
Enterprise Edition: any number of standard databases and composite databases

constraints.description: A database boundary is an administrative and transaction boundary, not sufficient evidence of secure multi-tenancy by itself.

indexingConsiderations: Choose vector dimensions, coordinate type, cosine or Euclidean similarity, quantization type, HNSW M, ef_construction, and the preview search-expansion factor only after measuring recall, latency, memory, disk, and population time.
Model nodes, relationships, labels, relationship types, identifiers, provenance, and embedding ownership before creating vector and full-text indexes.
Use native VECTOR values only where the selected Neo4j edition, store format, Cypher version, and driver path support them; otherwise use supported numeric-list properties.
Declare additional filterable properties in the vector-index schema when in-index filtering is required, and preserve their type and null semantics across ingestion.

For self-managed deployments, plan page cache, heap, persistent Lucene vector-index files, operating-system filesystem cache, transaction logs, replicas, backups, and graph traversal working sets together rather than treating Neo4j as a dedicated disk-oriented ANN system.
retrievalConsiderations: Evaluate vector-only, full-text-only, Cypher WRRF, neo4j-graphrag fusion, and Vector-Graph Composition on the same relevance set without treating graph traversal as lexical-vector hybrid retrieval.
Distinguish SEARCH-clause in-index filters from outer Cypher WHERE post-filters because they change result completeness and query cost.

Tune top-k, the preview vector.default_search_expansion_factor, quantization, full-text candidate windows, WRRF constants and weights, package fusion settings, and graph expansion depth under representative load.
Treat vector, full-text, and graph scores as source-specific signals; rank or calibrate them explicitly instead of comparing heterogeneous raw scores directly.
Measure vector-index freshness separately from transaction commit latency because changes made within the same transaction are not visible to the vector index.

limitations: Neo4j vector indexes use approximate nearest-neighbor search and can return fewer than the requested k results for large k values.
Only cosine and Euclidean similarity are configurable for vector indexes, and only one vector index can cover a given schema combination.
Changes made within the same transaction are not visible to the vector index, so ACID commit does not imply same-transaction vector-search visibility.
Binary quantization and vector.default_search_expansion_factor are Preview in Neo4j 2026.06; their maturity does not make the generally available vector-index capability Preview.

Community supports exactly one standard database, numeric-list vector properties, offline dump/load, and a smaller security and observability surface; Enterprise adds native VECTOR storage with block format, multiple or composite databases, clustering, online backup, advanced access control, and detailed metrics.

Standard Enterprise clustering synchronously replicates writes among enough primaries for commit, while read-scaling secondaries replicate asynchronously and can lag; bookmarks are required when causal read-after-write behavior matters.

Infinigraph property sharding requires a separate subscription, is not standard Enterprise replication, is unavailable on Aura, and has feature-specific limitations that must be tested with vector indexes and access controls.

Self-managed TLS is a Neo4j-core SSL-framework capability, while at-rest protection depends on separately configured host-platform volume encryption and does not establish Neo4j DBMS-core encryption at rest; Aura encryption remains inside the managed-service boundary.

AuraDB Free provides on-demand snapshot availability but has no documented restorable or exportable period; paid Aura snapshot cadence, retention, export, restore, access control, monitoring, customer-managed keys, and deployment isolation vary by plan.
The neo4j-graphrag 1.17.0 package and pure-Cypher WRRF are separate lexical-vector fusion origins, and neither should be conflated with Vector-Graph Composition.
Neo4j Community Edition is GPLv3, while Enterprise, Aura, and related services use commercial or service-specific terms.
usageGuidance: Use Neo4j when retrieval quality depends on both semantic similarity and explicit relationships, paths, provenance, or graph constraints.
Prefer a simpler vector store when graph traversal and relationship-aware context do not justify the additional modeling and operational surface.
Record Neo4j server, Cypher, vector-index provider, driver, neo4j-graphrag package, store format, Aura tier, and embedding-model versions for reproducibility.

Choose Community, Enterprise, Infinigraph, or an Aura plan from the required database count, VECTOR storage, access-control, TLS, host-volume encryption, monitoring, recovery, isolation, replication, and sharding boundaries before benchmarking retrieval.

Benchmark node and relationship vector indexes, filesystem-cache warm-up, filter selectivity, graph fan-out, Cypher WRRF, package fusion, security rules, bookmarks, secondary lag, and cluster routing on production-like data.

Exercise the scoped recovery path—Community offline dump/load, Enterprise online backup/restore, a paid Aura plan's documented export/restore actions, or AuraDB Free on-demand snapshots without an assumed restorable or exportable period—plus index rebuild and disaster recovery before treating Neo4j as authoritative RAG infrastructure.

claims.statement: Neo4j 2026.06 indexes numeric-list or eligible native VECTOR properties on nodes or relationships through Lucene HNSW with cosine or Euclidean similarity; scalar quantization is generally available, while binary quantization and vector.default_search_expansion_factor are Preview.
claims.rationale: The immutable 2026.06 Operations path and digest-bound Cypher 25 sources distinguish the generally available vector-index capability, edition-scoped VECTOR property storage, and the Preview maturity of two 2026.06 controls.

claims.statement: Neo4j Cypher 25 supports in-index vector filtering through SEARCH ... WHERE over declared filterable properties, while a normal outer WHERE acts as post-filtering and can return fewer than the requested neighbors.
claims.rationale: The SEARCH-clause documentation explicitly distinguishes in-index filtering from outer Cypher post-filtering and documents supported predicate and version boundaries.

claims.statement: Neo4j DBMS exposes vector indexes and full-text indexes that can be queried through Cypher, but combining their ranked outputs is not one automatic DBMS-core retrieval operation.
claims.rationale: Vector and full-text retrieval primitives are product capabilities, while their fusion boundary must be represented separately from the underlying indexes.

claims.statement: Neo4j Enterprise clustering uses replicated primaries and read-scaling secondaries, with topology and availability varying by edition and deployment.
claims.rationale: Cluster replication and read scaling are edition-scoped operational capabilities and must not be generalized to every Neo4j deployment.

claims.statement: Neo4j provides ACID database transactions, but vector-index updates are not visible to vector queries within the same transaction.
claims.rationale: Database transaction atomicity and vector-index query visibility are distinct guarantees and must be represented separately.

claims.statement: The first-party neo4j-graphrag 1.17.0 package can combine vector and full-text retrieval through configurable fusion or orchestration; this separately installed capability is package-scoped rather than DBMS-core.
claims.rationale: Vendor ownership does not make an independently installed and versioned first-party package part of the database engine; behavior is bound to the official 1.17.0 source at commit 7b69354.

claims.statement: Cypher can compose vector-search candidates with graph pattern matching and traversal to expand, constrain, connect, or contextualize retrieved entities.
claims.rationale: This behavior is Vector-Graph Composition implemented through query-language composition, not canonical dense-sparse hybrid retrieval.

claims.statement: Automatic data sharding is not a universal Neo4j capability; it is edition- or offering-specific and must be verified for the target deployment, including Infinigraph where applicable.
claims.rationale: Standard cluster replication must not be conflated with automatic data partitioning or sharding.

claims.statement: Community provides offline dump/load, Enterprise provides online full and differential backup/restore, paid Aura plans provide plan-specific snapshot, export, and restore actions, and AuraDB Free provides on-demand snapshots with no documented restorable or exportable period.
claims.rationale: Recovery behavior differs materially between self-managed editions, paid Aura plans, and AuraDB Free, whose official plan table records N/A for restorable and exportable periods.

claims.statement: Neo4j documentation describes Community Edition local and other self-managed installations as GPLv3, self-managed Enterprise editions as subject to commercial software terms, and Aura as governed by applicable cloud or self-service terms.
claims.rationale: Product licensing must be scoped separately from the Apache-2.0 license applying to the canonical RKM artifact, must cover both Local and Self Hosted installations, and must not assert an SPDX suffix not established by the cited edition source.

claims.statement: Neo4j documents a pure-Cypher lexical-vector hybrid pattern that independently ranks full-text and vector results and combines them with weighted reciprocal-rank fusion; it is a query-composition pattern rather than a separate index type.
claims.rationale: This first-party query-language path must remain distinct from the separately installed neo4j-graphrag package and from Vector-Graph Composition.

claims.statement: Neo4j 2026.06 labels vector.default_search_expansion_factor Preview and documents that values above 1.0 can trade additional query time for increased accuracy without changing the maturity of vector indexes as a whole.
claims.rationale: The subfeature requires its own Preview scope so its lifecycle status is not incorrectly inherited by or projected onto the enclosing vector capability.

claims.statement: Self-managed Neo4j 2026.06 vector indexes persist as Lucene-backed files that use the operating-system filesystem cache; cache misses can cause disk reads, so this behavior is not equivalent to a dedicated disk-oriented ANN architecture.
claims.rationale: Persistent files, cache residency, and cache-miss disk I/O are separate semantics and do not support a product-wide disk-backed-indexing boolean.

claims.statement: In an Enterprise cluster, primaries synchronously replicate enough writes before commit, secondaries replicate asynchronously and can lag, and bookmark-based routing provides causal read-after-write behavior when invoked.
claims.rationale: Transaction commit, secondary freshness, causal consistency, and vector-index visibility are different subsystem and topology guarantees.

claims.statement: Neo4j 2026.06 advanced RBAC and fine-grained privileges are Enterprise and applicable Aura-tier capabilities, while Community has a smaller security subset and sharded property databases exclude some property-based controls.
claims.rationale: Access control must be selected by edition, Aura tier, database topology, and indexed-retrieval behavior rather than through one aggregate rating.

claims.statement: Self-managed Neo4j provides product-core TLS through its SSL framework, while host platforms or operators separately provide storage-volume encryption rather than Neo4j DBMS-core at-rest encryption; Aura provides managed encryption for stored data, backups, inter-node traffic, and client connections.
claims.rationale: Product-core transport encryption, host-platform at-rest protection, and managed-service encryption have different implementation origins and responsibility boundaries.

claims.statement: Self-managed Neo4j provides basic server logs across editions, while detailed metrics and some query or security logs are Enterprise-scoped; external collection, dashboards, alerting, and Aura monitoring remain separate operational boundaries.
claims.rationale: Logs, Enterprise metrics, managed monitoring, and third-party observability are distinct facilities and cannot support one product-wide observability rating.

claims.statement: Community permits exactly one standard database, Enterprise permits multiple standard and composite databases, Infinigraph adds separately subscribed property sharding, and dedicated Aura network isolation is plan-specific rather than universal.
claims.rationale: Database count, composite access, sharding, and managed deployment isolation are different boundaries and do not establish generic multi-tenancy by themselves.

evidence.interpretation: The RKM profile can classify Neo4j as a graph database with native graph-based ANN and quantization rather than as a dedicated vector database.

evidence.summary: Neo4j's official hybrid-search guide provides pure-Cypher full-text and vector branches whose independently ranked outputs are combined with weighted reciprocal-rank fusion.
evidence.interpretation: The documented pattern supports lexical-vector hybrid retrieval through query-language composition without implying a separate hybrid index or automatic DBMS-core fusion operation.

sourceFragments.locator: Rank each source independently rather than comparing vector and full-text raw scores

limitations: The guide documents a composition pattern, not benchmarked relevance improvement or automatic selection of fusion parameters.
The mutable developer guide is bound to the HTML content SHA-256 captured on its recorded 2026-07-18 access date.

evidence.summary: Neo4j's vector-index memory documentation describes persistent Lucene index files, operating-system filesystem-cache residency, warming behavior, and disk reads under cache pressure or cold starts.
evidence.interpretation: The evidence supports explicit storage and cache semantics but not an unqualified disk-backed-indexing classification comparable to a dedicated disk-oriented ANN design.

sourceFragments.section: Vector index memory configuration; Optimal memory configuration for Neo4j with vector indexes
sourceFragments.locator: Lucene-backed files use OS filesystem cache; insufficient cache causes disk reads; physical index size is measured on disk; restart clears cache

limitations: The documentation provides capacity-planning guidance rather than workload-independent latency guarantees.
Aura storage and cache provisioning are provider managed and are not exposed with the same operator boundary.

evidence.summary: Neo4j edition, RBAC, and authorization-limit documentation scopes advanced privileges to Enterprise and applicable Aura tiers and identifies index-result behavior under security restrictions.
evidence.interpretation: Access-control capability and retrieval completeness must be evaluated by edition, Aura tier, topology, and query path rather than through an aggregate product rating.

limitations: Authorization features and limitations vary by control type, edition, Aura tier, Cypher version, and sharded topology.
Documentation does not replace threat modeling or access-control tests on the target data model.

evidence.summary: Neo4j self-managed security documentation identifies the Neo4j SSL framework for configurable TLS and separately directs operators to use host-platform volume encryption; Aura documentation states that stored data, backups, inter-node traffic, and client connections are encrypted.
evidence.interpretation: Product-core TLS, host-platform volume encryption, and managed-service encryption require separate capability origins and cannot support one product-wide encryption rating.

sourceFragments.locator: Host- or storage-volume encryption is an operator responsibility; TLS is recommended for Bolt, HTTPS, cluster, and backup channels
Configurable TLS for Bolt, HTTPS, cluster, and backup communication channels
Aura encryption at rest, intra-cluster encryption, required encrypted client connections, and encrypted backup buckets

limitations: Self-managed at-rest protection is not Neo4j DBMS-core encryption and its coverage and key lifecycle depend on the host platform and operator.
Self-managed TLS requires operator-managed certificates, trust, channel configuration, renewal, and rotation.
Aura customer-managed key availability depends on tier, provider, and region.

evidence.summary: Neo4j documentation distinguishes basic server logs from Enterprise-only detailed metrics and edition-specific query and security logging facilities.
evidence.interpretation: Logging and metrics are distinct observability surfaces, and externally operated collection or Aura monitoring must not be inferred from self-managed product documentation.

evidence.interpretation: Database administration, sharding, and dedicated managed-service isolation are separate boundaries and do not prove generic multi-tenancy or identical isolation across offerings.
